summary.headline: Maximus Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose about 52% YoY to INR59.91 crores, but EBITDA margin fell to 7.64% from 9.81% on Middle East war input costs.
summary.overview:
Consolidated revenue from operations was INR59.91 crores versus INR39.52 crores a year earlier, with EBITDA up about 18% to INR4.58 crores. Margin compression, attributed to higher input and freight costs from the ongoing Middle East war, and higher finance costs (INR1.53 crores vs INR0.92 crores) left PAT at INR2.05 crores versus INR2.33 crores a year ago. Management highlighted the proposed associate acquisition of Quebec Petroleum (40% stake), a Kenya grease plant planned for Q3 FY27, and a Tanzania warehousing expansion. Management guided to crossing about INR200 crores revenue in FY27 on a conservative basis.</overview>

segments.name: Manufacturing
segments.commentary: Highest EBITDA margin among the three verticals (manufacturing, toll blending, trading) in Q1 FY27 and historically. Operations in UAE and Kenya.

segments.name: Toll blending
segments.commentary: Management says it is being pursued aggressively; in talks with an East African MNC for toll blending.

segments.name: Trading
segments.commentary: Lowest-margin vertical per management. Long-term target split: manufacturing plus toll blending 75-80%, trading 20-25%.

segments.name: Specialty lubricants
segments.commentary: Contribute around 40% of topline, per CFO.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue expected to cross about INR200 crores on a conservative basis, with healthy EBITDA margins (stated even under the ongoing war scenario).
Margins expected to hold at current levels or improve over the next couple of quarters if supply disruption persists, through product mix diversification.
Kenya grease manufacturing facility planned for commissioning in Q3 FY27.
Tanzania expansion: initially warehousing and distribution, moving to manufacturing once scale is reached.
Recently launched modernisation programme: automated batch blending, additional storage and warehousing, improved filling lines, and capacity expansion at UAE and Kenya plants.
Capacity considered sufficient for next 2-3 years on single-shift basis; additional storage capex needed for full utilisation.
capex_capacity: Combined manufacturing capacity of about 50,000 KL across UAE and Kenya plants.
Capacity utilisation at about 45% across both units.
Kenya grease plant to cater to East African market, which has few grease manufacturers; also to support toll blending.
Proposed acquisition of an additional manufacturing unit as an associate; process underway, details to be shared later.
Quebec Petroleum: associate investment with initial 40% stake, aimed at entering the Indian domestic market.
demand_pricing: Management says demand for lubricants is supported by industrialisation, infrastructure, vehicle ownership and mining, power and construction; customers are shifting toward premium and specialty products.
Cited Middle East and Africa lubricant market growing from about USD 9.1 billion (2024) to USD 12.4 billion (2034).
Company serves more than 400 customers across 25+ countries and 50+ industries.
Top 10 customers account for roughly 70-75% of revenue, including distributors; company sells mainly through distributors, not B2C.
Product prices and landed costs (freight, insurance) rose due to the Middle East war; company passed on a partial cost increase, which also raised receivables.
Base oil and white oil prices are positively correlated with crude, with a lagged and non-identical impact on lubricant prices.
In Kenya, incumbents Shell and Total have not changed payment terms despite new entrants.

qa_highlights.question: How sensitive are margins to base oil and crude price movements?
qa_highlights.answer: Not directly coupled but positively correlated; raw materials (base oils and white oils) move in the same direction with a lag and not in the same proportion.

qa_highlights.question: Current utilisation of the 50,000 KL capacity, and targets over 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: About 45% utilised; capacity is sufficient for 2-3 years on a single shift, but full utilisation would need additional storage capex.

qa_highlights.question: Which vertical has the highest EBITDA margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Manufacturing, both in Q1 FY27 and historically; toll blending is being pursued more aggressively.

qa_highlights.question: Share of premium and specialty versus conventional revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Specialty lubricants contribute around 40% of topline.

qa_highlights.question: Why have receivables risen faster than revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Higher topline (about 50% growth), higher product prices and landed costs from the war, and partial pass-through of cost increases to selling prices.

qa_highlights.question: What if supply disruption lasts more than six months?
qa_highlights.answer: Management has onboarded new customers and broadened product baskets; margins may dip further but aim to hold or improve through diversification; still expects over INR200 crores revenue in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: How will Quebec Petroleum contribute?
qa_highlights.answer: Associate with 40% stake; its profits will be included in consolidated financials; focus is India domestic market, while Maximus covers Middle East, East and North Africa.

qa_highlights.question: Target revenue split between trading and toll blending over three years?
qa_highlights.answer: Manufacturing plus toll blending 75-80%, trading 20-25%; split between manufacturing and toll blending not disclosed as they overlap in co-branding.

qa_highlights.question: Concentration of revenue and B2B versus B2C mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Top 10 customers about 70-75% of revenue (distributors included); no own retail outlets; major revenue comes via distribution channels.

risks_watch: Margin compression: EBITDA margin down about 217 bps YoY to 7.64% due to input and freight costs from the Middle East war.
Working capital: receivables rising faster than revenue; financial cost up about 65% YoY to INR1.53 crores.
Customer concentration: top 10 customers about 70-75% of revenue.
Quebec Petroleum associate acquisition and additional manufacturing unit acquisition: terms and financials not yet disclosed.
Competitive response in Kenya from incumbents such as Shell and Total; payment terms unchanged so far.
Management did not split revenue between manufacturing and toll blending; the reported Q1 PAT decline despite revenue growth needs monitoring.
